comments.rawMarkdown:
Depends on the criticality, for internal apps used by colleagues I just vibe code away, as long as it works and they are happy its fine. 
For production or security exposure I still review the most critical parts, today Codex and Claude where not able to solve a pagation problem for an API is use to retrieve term base entries, they always ended in death loop prompts, so i wrote the critical part for the offset in the client class myself, took me some time to read the whole documentation :/

Same applies for kaggle, for most part I vibe code, but sometimes codex, which i use on my private machine, gets stuck and you either have to write it yourself or guide it to unstuck itself. And i agree thats the bottleneck.
But its also way more fun than a year ago, if i have a fun app idea i can just vibecode it, no more learning matlibplot syntax, or regex, or all the other extremly straining package bs.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown: Since everyone is using agents to code now, the question is: do you spend more or less time Kaggling as a result? For me, I just do more stuff in parallel (work, Kaggle etc), and I had to change my mental model of training models: from doing it myself to supervising. Event frontier models sometimes make really fatal mistakes, so I need to understand the whole project anyway... which means human cognition is still the bottleneck (at least for me).
